frequency_question: How often do executive principals successfully push through a controversial Senate confirmation within a narrow time window?
membership_rule: Includes all Cabinet-level or major regulatory agency nominations (e.g., FDA, CDC, EPA, Cabinet secretaries) submitted or pushed to a floor vote with high presidential intent during periods of tight legislative calendars since 2000. Excludes uncontroversial routine judicial or ambassador confirmations.

cases.name: Marty Makary or similar recent high-level health nominations pushed late

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 6 named; believed roughly 7 in total for high-priority FDA/health agency confirmations under pressure.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-agency appointments that lack executive-level push.
skeleton: Presidents pushing high-priority health agency nominees through the Senate since 2000, decomposed by administration urgency and ultimate delivery capability.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 7 total tracked prominent contested health nominee pushes where the executive had strong will to deliver.
validity_reason: Relies on the current structural dynamics of Senate confirmation powers and executive appointment authority, remaining stable until the next presidential term shift.
